items.title: Ray Conniff interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 14, 1998
items.q: Did you by the way see — who’s the great fellow, the interviewer, the top interviewer on CNN, what’s his name? >> [INTERVIEWER] Not Ted Koppel. [INTERVIEWEE] No, no, no, no. Larry King.

ctx.x: Oh boy do I wish I had that today, yeah. For one dollar, what an investment. And of course I used it for a while as a transposing device, but that led me into writing, because later on I studied and I would, I started with Hugo Friedhofer, by the way, boy he was great. Do you remember him? He wrote for the motion pictures out here on the west coast. And then I ran into, who was it, somebody tipped me off to start looking into the classics, and I started taking Tchaikovsky’s scores — did you ever do that? You take…

No, no, no, no. Larry King. He had Eric Clapton on. And he was playing guitar, and I think except the way I heard him and his writings with the guitar, mainly today, well a point I want to make is a lot of today’s music is being written by guitar players. You can’t — with the guitar you miss the beauty of a Tchaikovsky, like [scats], you know the third in the bass. The seventh and the bass. With a guitar you always have the tonic in the bass. And I think that’s missing a little bit in the younger writers today.…
